items.title: Don Menza and Sam Noto interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, January 28, 1997
items.q: David Rose is mentioned only as a colleague/friend of Henry Mancini ('Pete Rugolo, David Rose and there’s somebody else and Mancini. They were all in Hawaii...') and as someone the interviewee's wife 'Rose' knew ('Rose loved him'). The interviewee does not describe a direct personal or professional

ctx.x: —you had a lot of studio work.

Oh, yeah. And I have to say one of the really great thrills of my life was working with Henry Mancini, and I sorely miss him. And he was exactly like his music. He made a big influence, a huge influence on me, like so far as my writing, arranging, seeing him in front of an orchestra. The great, great story from Mancini is when Pavarotti did his movie, I asked Hank, I said, and on his birth certificate it says Enrico, his real name was Enrico. I said, “Hank,” I said, “you going to do the movie?” He said, “Oh, no,…

movie. Three years later, we’re celebrating, my wife and I are celebrating our twenty- fifth anniversary and we’re in San Francisco. We check into the hotel and here’s this little flowers and champagne and the whole thing. And Hank calls me and he said, “You going to come with me to rehearsal?” I said, “Well Rose is with me.” He says, “I know, bring her.” He said, “I’ve got to talk to you.” I said, “You want to talk to me?” I wonder what for?
